lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 108, which makes CI edit its PR comments only when a result changes.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one oh eight, which makes CI edit its pull request comments only when a result changes.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Each time a job finishes, it calls the summary script.
The script compares a hidden results marker with the one already in the summary.
If they match, it skips the edit. If a result changed, it edits once, with a link to verify.
The key screenshot pair and the shots table now live only in the verify comment.
Closed review findings keep a short summary and no detail.
And every comment edit now logs its size, so the savings can be measured.
A watching session gets the whole comment on every edit. On PR 102 that was about 50 big edits, mostly "still running".
lines.say: A watching session gets the whole comment on every edit. On pull request one oh two, that was about fifty big edits, mostly still running.

lines.caption: The key idea: if the results marker hasn't changed, nothing that matters changed, so CI leaves the comment alone.
Every job that writes a comment calls the summary script, and the summary job calls it last.
The marker holds the head commit and a short hash of every finished check, the verify note and the run.
So a run posts "running" once per head, then edits only when a check passes or fails.
The verify comment, written once per run, shows the key result and the shots table near its top.
Settled findings shrink, while open, accepted and new ones stay whole for the digest agent.
The comment script's log line now ends with the comment's length in characters.
Before, the summary repeated every table on every job. Now it's a checks table and one link.
The hidden markers other tools read are all kept.
The PR changes four CI scripts, one line of the digest agent, CLAUDE.md, and adds this page.
To undo it, revert the PR, and the summary is written on every call again.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built against the problem measured on PR 102, and the markers its readers need.
lines.say: It was built against the problem measured on pull request one oh two, and the markers its readers need.

lines.caption: The building session ran the verify comment script on a fake run: the new layout came out in order.
A dry run of the summary wrote once, then skipped the identical second pass.
The scripts compile.
There's no Thunar test, since no Thunar code changed, and CI on this PR hasn't run yet.
A fresh review agent found three low findings before the first push, all fixed in the second commit.
They were about stale links, unmarked old shots, and a dry run that printed nothing.
CI's own review reports in the code review comment on the PR.
The issue's real test, counting edits and their size, runs on this PR's CI and is reported in a comment.
Other PRs get the quieter comments once this is on main.
Links to the PR, the issue and CI's comments are here.
Part 3. What comes later: nothing builds on it yet.
The next step is this PR's own measurement, posted as a PR comment.
In short: CI's PR comments now change only when a result does, and the big tables are written once.
